resource.name: aws_sagemaker_domain
resource.description: Provides a SageMaker AI Domain resource.
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_sagemaker_domain` Terraform resource enables the creation and management of a SageMaker Domain, which serves as a foundational environment for machine learning workflows in AWS. It is commonly used to set up secure, scalable infrastructure for data scientists and ML practitioners, including user profiles, shared storage, and access control for SageMaker Studio. Key configurations include authentication methods (such as IAM or SSO), network settings, lifecycle policies, and resource sharing, making it ideal for orchestrating collaborative AI development environments.

examples.title: Basic usage
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an AWS SageMaker Domain with IAM authentication, specifying a VPC and subnets for network isolation. It includes the setup of a default user execution role using an `aws_iam_role` resource and an `aws_iam_policy_document` to define the trust relationship for SageMaker service access.

examples.title: Using Custom Images
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an `aws_sagemaker_domain` with custom images for kernel gateway applications by integrating `aws_sagemaker_image`, `aws_sagemaker_app_image_config`, and `aws_sagemaker_image_version` resources. It highlights the use of the `custom_image` block within `default_user_settings` to specify a custom app image configuration and image version, enabling tailored SageMaker environments.

arguments.name: app_network_access_type
arguments.description: (Optional) Specifies the VPC used for non-EFS traffic. The default value is `PublicInternetOnly`. Valid values are `PublicInternetOnly` and `VpcOnly`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `app_network_access_type` argument for the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource allows users to specify the network access configuration for SageMaker Studio applications, controlling whether non-EFS traffic is routed through the public internet (`PublicInternetOnly`) or a private VPC (`VpcOnly`). This setting impacts the security and connectivity of the environment, enabling users to align network access with their organization's requirements for public or private infrastructure.

arguments.name: app_security_group_management
arguments.description: (Optional) The entity that creates and manages the required security groups for inter-app communication in `VPCOnly` mode. Valid values are `Service` and `Customer`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `app_security_group_management` argument in the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource allows users to specify whether the security groups required for inter-application communication in `VPCOnly` mode are managed by AWS (`Service`) or manually configured by the user (`Customer`). This setting impacts the level of control over network security, enabling users to either rely on AWS-managed defaults or define custom security group configurations to meet specific compliance or networking requirements.

arguments.name: auth_mode
arguments.description: (Required) The mode of authentication that members use to access the domain. Valid values are `IAM` and `SSO`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `auth_mode` argument in the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource specifies the authentication method users must use to access the SageMaker domain, allowing you to control whether access is managed via AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) or Single Sign-On (SSO). Setting this argument defines the domain's access control mechanism, aligning with organizational security policies and user management preferences.

arguments.name: domain_name
arguments.description: (Required) The domain name.
arguments.llm_summary: The `domain_name` argument specifies the unique name of the SageMaker Domain, serving as an identifier for the domain within the AWS environment. This is a required parameter that enables users to define and manage a centralized environment for machine learning development, including user profiles, shared resources, and security configurations.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument for the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource allows users to specify a unique identifier for the SageMaker domain, typically used to reference or manage the resource programmatically within Terraform configurations. While optional, setting this argument can help ensure consistent tracking and integration of the domain across workflows or external systems.

arguments.name: kms_key_id
arguments.description: (Optional) The AWS KMS customer managed CMK used to encrypt the EFS volume attached to the domain.
arguments.llm_summary: The `kms_key_id` argument for the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource allows users to specify the AWS KMS customer-managed key (CMK) used to encrypt the EFS volume attached to the SageMaker domain. By configuring this argument, users can enhance data security and compliance by defining custom encryption for storage associated with the domain.

arguments.name: subnet_ids
arguments.description: (Required) The VPC subnets that Studio uses for communication.
arguments.llm_summary: The `subnet_ids` argument for the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource specifies the set of VPC subnets that Amazon SageMaker Studio will use for network communication. By defining these subnets, users control the network environment for Studio, ensuring secure and isolated connectivity within their VPC, which is essential for managing data flow and integrating with other AWS services.

arguments.name: tag_propagation
arguments.description: (Optional) Indicates whether custom tag propagation is supported for the domain. Defaults to `DISABLED`. Valid values are: `ENABLED` and `DISABLED`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `tag_propagation` argument for the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource allows users to control whether custom tags applied to the domain are automatically propagated to resources created within the domain. Setting this argument to `ENABLED` facilitates consistent tag management across related resources, supporting use cases like cost allocation, resource organization, and compliance tracking, while `DISABLED` prevents tag inheritance.

arguments.name: tags
arguments.description: (Optional) A map of tags to assign to the resource. If configured with a provider `default_tags` configuration block present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level.
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags` argument for the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource allows users to define a map of key-value pairs to assign metadata to the SageMaker domain, enabling resource categorization, organization, and cost tracking. By setting this argument, users can streamline management tasks such as identifying environments (e.g., "dev" or "prod"), applying governance policies, or integrating with billing and reporting workflows.

arguments.name: tags_all
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags_all` argument for the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource allows users to define a comprehensive set of key-value tags that are automatically merged with resource-specific tags, enabling consistent metadata management across AWS resources. By configuring this argument, users can streamline tagging for cost allocation, access control, and resource organization, aligning the SageMaker domain with broader tagging strategies in their cloud environment.

arguments.name: vpc_id
arguments.description: (Required) The ID of the Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) that Studio uses for communication. The following arguments are optional:
arguments.llm_summary: The `vpc_id` argument specifies the ID of the Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) that SageMaker Studio uses for network communication, ensuring that all traffic between the Studio environment and other AWS services or resources remains within the defined VPC. This configuration is essential for users aiming to enforce network isolation, enhance security, and control access to resources in compliance with their organization's networking policies.

blocks.name: default_space_settings
blocks.description: (Required) The default space settings. See `default_space_settings` Block below.

arguments.name: execution_role
arguments.description: (Required) The execution role for the space.
arguments.llm_summary: The `execution_role` argument specifies the IAM role that SageMaker uses to execute actions within the default user space of the domain, such as accessing AWS resources or managing workloads. Setting this required role ensures proper permissions for running machine learning tasks and interacting with associated services, aligning with user goals of securing and enabling resource access in SageMaker environments.

arguments.name: security_groups
arguments.description: (Optional) The security groups for the Amazon Virtual Private Cloud that the space uses for communication.
arguments.llm_summary: The `security_groups` argument in the `default_space_settings` of the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource allows users to specify a set of security group IDs that control network access for the Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) associated with the space. By configuring this argument, users can define inbound and outbound traffic rules to enhance security, restrict communication, and meet compliance requirements for the SageMaker environment.

blocks.name: custom_file_system_config
blocks.description: (Optional) The settings for assigning a custom file system to a user profile. Permitted users can access this file system in Amazon SageMaker AI Studio. See `custom_file_system_config` Block below.

blocks.name: efs_file_system_config
blocks.description: (Optional) The default EBS storage settings for a private space. See `efs_file_system_config` Block below.

arguments.name: file_system_id
arguments.description: (Required) The ID of your Amazon EFS file system.
arguments.llm_summary: The `file_system_id` argument specifies the unique identifier of an Amazon EFS file system to integrate with the SageMaker Domain's `efs_file_system_config`. By defining this ID, users enable persistent storage for SageMaker notebooks and applications, facilitating seamless data access and retention across sessions, which is essential for managing shared datasets or collaborative workflows.

arguments.name: file_system_path
arguments.description: (Required) The path to the file system directory that is accessible in Amazon SageMaker AI Studio. Permitted users can access only this directory and below.
arguments.llm_summary: The `file_system_path` argument specifies the directory path within the Amazon EFS file system that is accessible to users in SageMaker Studio, effectively defining the root directory for user access and isolating their file system interactions to this path and its subdirectories. By setting this argument, users can control the scope of file system access for SageMaker Studio environments, ensuring secure and organized data management aligned with their workflows.

blocks.llm_summary: The `efs_file_system_config` block within the `custom_file_system_config` of the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource defines the configuration for integrating an Amazon EFS (Elastic File System) as the default storage for private spaces in SageMaker. This block enables users to specify and manage EFS-related settings, such as file system details and mount options, providing scalable, shared storage for machine learning environments and ensuring seamless data access across users and applications.

The `custom_file_system_config` block within the `default_space_settings` of the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource enables the configuration of a custom file system for user profiles in Amazon SageMaker Studio, allowing permitted users to access shared or personalized storage for AI and ML workflows. This block encapsulates settings related to file system integration, providing users with fine-grained control over storage access and customization to support collaborative or specialized data processing needs.

blocks.name: custom_posix_user_config
blocks.description: (Optional) Details about the POSIX identity that is used for file system operations. See `custom_posix_user_config` Block below.

arguments.name: gid
arguments.description: (Optional) The POSIX group ID.
arguments.llm_summary: The `gid` argument in the `custom_posix_user_config` block of the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource allows users to specify the POSIX group ID for the SageMaker user profile's underlying file system. By setting this value, users can control group-level permissions and access for files and directories, ensuring compatibility with POSIX-compliant systems and enabling secure multi-user collaboration within SageMaker environments.

arguments.name: uid
arguments.description: (Optional) The POSIX user ID.
arguments.llm_summary: The `uid` argument in the `custom_posix_user_config` block of the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource allows users to define the POSIX user ID (UID) for the SageMaker domain's associated user profile. By specifying this numeric identifier, users can control the mapping of SageMaker user profiles to POSIX-based systems, ensuring compatibility with file permissions, access control, and identity management in environments that rely on POSIX standards.

blocks.llm_summary: The `custom_posix_user_config` block within the `default_space_settings` of the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource defines the POSIX identity (e.g., user ID and group ID) used for file system operations in SageMaker environments. This configuration enables precise control over file access and permissions, ensuring compatibility with POSIX-compliant systems and facilitating secure and efficient data handling for custom workloads.

blocks.name: jupyter_lab_app_settings
blocks.description: (Optional) The settings for the JupyterLab application. See `jupyter_lab_app_settings` Block below.

arguments.name: built_in_lifecycle_config_arn
arguments.description: (Optional) The lifecycle configuration that runs before the default lifecycle configuration. It can override changes made in the default lifecycle configuration.
arguments.llm_summary: The `built_in_lifecycle_config_arn` argument for the `jupyter_lab_app_settings` in the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource allows users to specify the ARN of a pre-defined lifecycle configuration that executes prior to the default lifecycle configuration. This enables customization of initialization processes, such as setting environment variables or preloading dependencies, to override or augment default behaviors in JupyterLab environments.

arguments.name: lifecycle_config_arns
arguments.description: (Optional) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Lifecycle Configurations.
arguments.llm_summary: The `lifecycle_config_arns` argument in the `jupyter_lab_app_settings` block of the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource allows users to specify a set of Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) for Lifecycle Configurations that define custom behaviors or actions for JupyterLab environments, such as resource initialization, cleanup, or automation tasks. By setting this argument, users can streamline environment management, enforce consistent configurations, and optimize workflows within SageMaker JupyterLab instances.

blocks.name: app_lifecycle_management
blocks.description: (Optional) Indicates whether idle shutdown is activated for JupyterLab applications. see `app_lifecycle_management` Block below.

blocks.name: idle_settings
blocks.description: (Optional) Settings related to idle shutdown of Studio applications. see `idle_settings` Block below.

arguments.name: idle_timeout_in_minutes
arguments.description: (Optional) The time that SageMaker AI waits after the application becomes idle before shutting it down. Valid values are between `60` and `525600`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `idle_timeout_in_minutes` argument for the `idle_settings` block in the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource allows users to define the duration (in minutes) that SageMaker waits before automatically shutting down idle applications. By configuring this timeout, users can optimize resource utilization and cost management by controlling the lifecycle of idle applications within the SageMaker environment.

arguments.name: lifecycle_management
arguments.description: (Optional) Indicates whether idle shutdown is activated for the application type. Valid values are `ENABLED` and `DISABLED`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `lifecycle_management` argument in the `idle_settings` block of the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource allows users to control whether idle shutdown is activated for SageMaker applications, enabling automated lifecycle management for resource optimization. By setting this argument to `ENABLED` or `DISABLED`, users can define the application's behavior during idle periods, helping to reduce costs and improve efficiency by shutting down unused resources.

arguments.name: max_idle_timeout_in_minutes
arguments.description: (Optional) The maximum value in minutes that custom idle shutdown can be set to by the user. Valid values are between `60` and `525600`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `max_idle_timeout_in_minutes` argument for the `idle_settings` in the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource allows users to define the maximum duration (in minutes) that a SageMaker environment can remain idle before shutting down, ensuring efficient resource utilization and cost management. By setting this value, users can control the upper limit for custom idle shutdown configurations, balancing operational flexibility with automated resource cleanup.

arguments.name: min_idle_timeout_in_minutes
arguments.description: (Optional) The minimum value in minutes that custom idle shutdown can be set to by the user. Valid values are between `60` and `525600`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `min_idle_timeout_in_minutes` argument for the `idle_settings` in the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource allows users to define the minimum allowable duration (in minutes) for custom idle shutdown settings in SageMaker environments. By configuring this value, users can enforce a lower limit on idle timeout periods, ensuring resource optimization and cost control while maintaining flexibility for user-defined idle behavior within the specified range (60 to 525600 minutes).

blocks.llm_summary: The `idle_settings` block in the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource under "app_lifecycle_management" configures parameters for automatically shutting down idle Studio applications, optimizing resource usage and cost management. It encapsulates settings related to idle timeout behavior, enabling users to enforce lifecycle policies that prevent unnecessary resource consumption during periods of inactivity.

The `app_lifecycle_management` block within the `jupyter_lab_app_settings` configuration of the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource enables control over the lifecycle behavior of JupyterLab applications, specifically managing idle shutdown settings to optimize resource usage. By configuring this block, users can automate application shutdown during idle periods, reducing costs and improving operational efficiency in SageMaker environments.

blocks.name: code_repository
blocks.description: (Optional) A list of Git repositories that SageMaker AI automatically displays to users for cloning in the JupyterServer application. see `code_repository` Block below.

arguments.name: repository_url
arguments.description: (Optional) The URL of the Git repository.
arguments.llm_summary: The `repository_url` argument for the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource's `code_repository` configuration specifies the URL of a Git repository that serves as the source for code and artifacts used in SageMaker workflows. By setting this required argument, users can integrate version-controlled code into their SageMaker environment, enabling reproducible machine learning experiments, streamlined collaboration, and automated deployment pipelines.

blocks.llm_summary: The `code_repository` block within the `jupyter_lab_app_settings` configuration of the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource specifies a list of Git repositories that are automatically displayed to users in the JupyterServer application for cloning and use in their SageMaker environment. This block enables streamlined access to pre-defined code repositories, facilitating collaborative development, reproducibility, and efficient setup of machine learning workflows directly within JupyterLab.

blocks.name: custom_image
blocks.description: (Optional) A list of custom SageMaker AI images that are configured to run as a JupyterLab app. see `custom_image` Block below.

arguments.name: app_image_config_name
arguments.description: (Required) The name of the App Image Config.
arguments.llm_summary: The `app_image_config_name` argument specifies the name of the App Image Config associated with a custom image in an Amazon SageMaker Domain, allowing users to define runtime configurations such as environment variables, kernel settings, or file system mappings for their applications. Setting this argument ensures the custom image is properly configured to meet specific application requirements during execution within the SageMaker environment.

arguments.name: image_name
arguments.description: (Required) The name of the Custom Image.
arguments.llm_summary: The `image_name` argument specifies the unique name of a custom image to be used within the SageMaker Domain, enabling users to define and reference a specific containerized environment for their machine learning workflows. By setting this required value, users can ensure their SageMaker notebooks or applications utilize the desired pre-configured software stack or dependencies tailored to their project needs.

arguments.name: image_version_number
arguments.description: (Optional) The version number of the Custom Image.
arguments.llm_summary: "Defines the version number of the custom image associated with the SageMaker Domain, allowing users to specify which iteration of the image to use for their machine learning environment. This enables precise control over the software stack and dependencies, supporting reproducibility and compatibility in model development workflows."

blocks.llm_summary: The `custom_image` block within the `jupyter_lab_app_settings` configuration of the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource allows users to define a list of custom SageMaker AI images tailored for running JupyterLab applications. This block encapsulates settings for specifying custom container images, enabling users to customize the runtime environment for JupyterLab, such as pre-installed libraries, tools, or frameworks, to meet specific data science or machine learning requirements.

blocks.name: default_resource_spec
blocks.description: (Optional) The default instance type and the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the SageMaker AI image created on the instance. see `default_resource_spec` Block below.

arguments.name: instance_type
arguments.description: (Optional) The instance type that the image version runs on.. For valid values see SageMaker AI Instance Types.
arguments.llm_summary: The `instance_type` argument in the `default_resource_spec` of the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource allows users to specify the compute instance type for running the associated image version. By configuring this argument, users can tailor the underlying hardware resources (e.g., CPU, GPU, memory) to match the performance requirements of their SageMaker workloads, enabling efficient execution of machine learning tasks or applications.

arguments.name: lifecycle_config_arn
arguments.description: (Optional) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Lifecycle Configuration attached to the Resource.
arguments.llm_summary: The `lifecycle_config_arn` argument allows users to specify the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of a SageMaker Lifecycle Configuration to associate with the default resource specification in the `aws_sagemaker_domain`. This enables the automation of custom setup or teardown scripts for resources, such as notebook instances, improving environment initialization and management workflows.

arguments.name: sagemaker_image_arn
arguments.description: (Optional) The ARN of the SageMaker AI image that the image version belongs to.
arguments.llm_summary: The `sagemaker_image_arn` argument in the `default_resource_spec` of the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource allows users to specify the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of a SageMaker AI image associated with the image version to be used for the domain's default compute environment. By setting this argument, users can define the base container image for machine learning workloads, enabling customization of runtime environments for training or inference tasks.

arguments.name: sagemaker_image_version_alias
arguments.description: (Optional) The SageMaker AI Image Version Alias.
arguments.llm_summary: The `sagemaker_image_version_alias` argument allows users to specify a version alias for the SageMaker-provided AI image used in the `default_resource_spec` configuration of an `aws_sagemaker_domain`. By setting this value, users can control which version of the SageMaker image is utilized, enabling consistent and predictable runtime environments for their machine learning workloads.

arguments.name: sagemaker_image_version_arn
arguments.description: (Optional) The ARN of the image version created on the instance.
arguments.llm_summary: The `sagemaker_image_version_arn` argument in the `default_resource_spec` of the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource allows users to specify the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of a specific SageMaker image version to be used for the instance. By setting this argument, users can control the runtime environment for their SageMaker domain, enabling customization of pre-configured container images for machine learning workflows, such as defining software dependencies or frameworks.

blocks.llm_summary: The `default_resource_spec` block within the `jupyter_lab_app_settings` configuration of the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource defines the default compute instance type and the SageMaker AI image (via its Amazon Resource Name) used for JupyterLab environments. This block enables users to customize the underlying infrastructure and runtime environment for JupyterLab applications, ensuring optimal performance and compatibility for machine learning workflows.

blocks.name: emr_settings
blocks.description: (Optional) The configuration parameters that specify the IAM roles assumed by the execution role of SageMaker AI (assumable roles) and the cluster instances or job execution environments (execution roles or runtime roles) to manage and access resources required for running Amazon EMR clusters or Amazon EMR Serverless applications. see `emr_settings` Block below.

arguments.name: assumable_role_arns
arguments.description: (Optional) An array of Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) of the IAM roles that the execution role of SageMaker AI can assume for performing operations or tasks related to Amazon EMR clusters or Amazon EMR Serverless applications. These roles define the permissions and access policies required when performing Amazon EMR-related operations, such as listing, connecting to, or terminating Amazon EMR clusters or Amazon EMR Serverless applications. They are typically used in cross-account access scenarios, where the Amazon EMR resources (clusters or serverless applications) are located in a different AWS account than the SageMaker AI domain.
arguments.llm_summary: The `assumable_role_arns` argument in the `emr_settings` block of the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource allows users to specify a set of IAM role ARNs that the SageMaker execution role can assume to perform operations on Amazon EMR clusters or EMR Serverless applications. This configuration enables cross-account access and ensures SageMaker has the necessary permissions to interact with EMR resources, supporting workflows that require integration between SageMaker and EMR for data processing or machine learning tasks.

arguments.name: execution_role_arns
arguments.description: (Optional) An array of Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) of the IAM roles used by the Amazon EMR cluster instances or job execution environments to access other AWS services and resources needed during the runtime of your Amazon EMR or Amazon EMR Serverless workloads, such as Amazon S3 for data access, Amazon CloudWatch for logging, or other AWS services based on the particular workload requirements.
arguments.llm_summary: The `execution_role_arns` argument in the `emr_settings` block of the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource allows users to specify a set of IAM role ARNs that grant Amazon EMR cluster instances or job execution environments the necessary permissions to access AWS services and resources during runtime. Configuring this argument ensures seamless integration with services like Amazon S3 for data storage, Amazon CloudWatch for monitoring, and other AWS resources required for EMR workloads, aligning with workload-specific access requirements.

blocks.llm_summary: The `emr_settings` block within the `jupyter_lab_app_settings` configuration of the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource defines IAM role parameters for integrating Amazon EMR clusters or EMR Serverless applications with SageMaker. It encapsulates settings for execution and runtime roles, enabling secure resource access and management required for running distributed data processing or machine learning workflows in EMR environments. Configuring this block allows users to seamlessly connect SageMaker JupyterLab environments with EMR, facilitating scalable data processing and analytics.

The `jupyter_lab_app_settings` block within the `default_space_settings` of the `aws_sagemaker_domain` resource configures environment-specific settings for the JupyterLab application, enabling tailored user experiences and resource management for data science workflows. This block encapsulates related configurations such as default resource limits, security settings, and application behavior, allowing users to optimize the JupyterLab environment for collaborative machine learning and analysis tasks.
